alex.yang: Quick heads-up: profiling run of the mixed-precision bundle (FP8 primary, INT8 fallback, 4-bit optional) shows a ~12% latency regression at batch=8 vs baseline float16 on A100.

maria.perez: Ugh. did you run the kernel selector trace? could be choosing FP8 GEMM kernel that is slower on that sequence length.

alex.yang: Yep, attaching trace snippet from perfprof:
```
selected_kernel: fp8_gemm_tiled
seq_len: 128
tokens/s: 45k
fallback: false
latencies_ms: [1.2,1.1,1.35]
```

sam.choi: What's the input distribution? batching heuristic might be packing unevenly causing small micro-batches.

alex.yang: Input median len 64, p95 256. batching policy is dynamic with max_batch=16, timeout=8ms. saw lots of small KV cache hits causing extra copies.

chen.wu: Can you rerun with `--quant-calibration=perlayer` vs `global`? FP8 calibration can change kernel path & perf.

alex.yang: Quick A/B:
- global calibr -> +12% reg
- perlayer calibr -> -3% (3% faster than baseline)
So calibration affects kernel selection.

maria.perez: Did you try excluding embeddings/lm_head from quant? those are sensitive and can affect memory layout.

alex.yang: Excluded embedding + lm_head (kept fp16) -> latency dropped and eval quality stable.

sam.choi: Sounds like partial quantization wins. propose heuristic: keep embeddings & lm_head fp16 and first/last transformer blocks fp16 if calibration variance > threshold.

chen.wu: Also add a profiler hook to log kernel id and tensor dtype per layer, so we can correlate.

infra-bot: perf-ci: build 1289 completed. diff report: batch=8 p50 +9.8% -> investigating.

maria.perez: Plan: alex to add per-layer dtype logging + rerun with perlayer calibration & embedding exclusion; sam to prototype heuristic; chen to add trace fields. Sync tomorrow.

alex.yang: On it. will push small runtime patch `log_kernels=1` and attach output here.

sam.choi: :thumbsup:
